sections.text: Who is indifferent to praise and censure, who enjoys silence, who is contented with every fate, who has no fixed abode, who is steadfast in mind, and filled with devotion, such a one is My beloved.
Verily those who love the spiritual wisdom as I have taught, whose faith never fails, and who concentrate their whole nature on Me, they indeed are My most beloved.

What is my purpose and destiny? Weve been discussing chapter 12, bhakti yoga. Devotion is love for the Divine. Love is nothing but identification.
The more we identify with someone, the more we like that person. When identification becomes complete, we say we fell in love with that person. So bhakti is nothing but the love for the divine.
Love cannot occur without knowledge of that person or knowledge of that thing. So in this case, loving God is not possible without knowing God. Knowledge is as important as my desire to love God.
The knowledge about God, the knowledge about the Supreme Being, is what we had been learning from Bhagavan. In the last five chapters, from chapter 7 through 11, Bhagavan elaborated the nature of the Supreme. In chapter seven he says, there is nothing greater than Me.
And then he explains that everything you see is nothing but me -- the prakriti you see is nothing but my lower Prakriti, my lower nature, the manifest Prakriti. So he has described his lower Prakriti as the manifest world which we see. We complain that we have not seen Bhagavan.
But Bhagavan said, you see me every day. You deal with me every day. You just do not know that you are dealing with Bhagavan, because there is nothing other than me in this world.
Then he described many aspects of this Prakriti -- how we can identify his presence in Prakriti, which we saw in chapter 10, Vibhuti Yoga: anything excellent you see in this world, consider that to be my presence. I am the strength in the strong, the intelligence in the intellect, the fragrance in the flower. Everything that right now I consider to be something other than me -- Bhagavan said -- is me, the supreme alone.
Right now, my identification is so complete with this limited self. I consider this body, mind, and intellect to be me. This identity is so complete that loving myself is very easy.
In spite of all my shortcomings that I am aware of, I never hate myself, because the identification is so complete that Im in love with myself. But once again, the quest in life is to change this identification from this limited self to the supreme self. For that to happen, I obviously need to know Bhagavan.
As we have seen in the last five chapters, Bhagavan has been telling us the nature of the supreme. In chapter 11, just before this chapter, Bhagavan demonstrated that everything comes out of me and everything merges into me -- whether you consider it good, bad, or ugly. Its easy for us to associate divinity with something pristine and sattvic.
But its very difficult for our mind to associate divinity with something that doesnt align with us, that is not conducive to our comfort. Therefore, in this chapter, Bhagavan, while explaining Bhakti, describes the nature of the perfect devotee. From the beginning of this chapter we saw Arjunas question: which is better? One who worships the manifest Prakriti, the manifest nature of God, or those who worship the supreme without any attributes? Because in the end we have learned that he does not have any form.
He is not a man, not a woman, not it, not she, not he -- hes everything. Without any form, it is very difficult for us to grasp his nature. That higher Prakriti, Bhagavan said, is very different from the manifest Prakriti which you see.
But to focus on that higher Prakriti, my mind may not be capable. Bhagavan said, for those who consider themselves identified with this body -- the embodied ones who consider this is me -- As we said, our identity is so complete with this body, mind, and intellect. Nobody has to tell me this is me or thats me -- the rest is the world outside.
For one who considers himself thus, to focus his mind on the unmanifest is very difficult. Klesha Adhikatarah Tesham -- for them the difficulty is much greater. So for them it is easier to focus on one form that they find divine.
Ramakrishna, or any great Mahatma -- in their presence, you dont have to figure out what God looks like. Many children in our neighborhood, when Gurudev came to our house, would say, God came to Bhatts house. Because we easily associate divinity with such a person. Bhagavan said, this may be easier for you, Arjuna.
At your level, the easiest way to worship me is to give your mind and intellect to me. In other words, synchronize your mind and intellect with me. As we discussed last time -- WWKD, What Would Krishna Do in this situation? Like the Christian bracelets that say WWJD.
Its for teenagers who are facing peer pressure -- should I smoke or not smoke? You say, think about it. Look at the bracelet: WWJD. What would Jesus do in this case? Synchronize your mind and intellect with me.
Give your mind and intellect to me and make me the supreme goal. Ill take care of everything. If that is not possible, Bhagavan gives another option: constant practice or constant learning of the nature of the Lord from the scriptures.
If that is not possible, give me all your actions -- work for me and do all your actions for me. My employer is Lord Krishna. Everything I do is for him.
If even that is not possible, then just do Karma Phala Tyaga -- dont expect anything from what you do. In the end he said, Karma Phala Tyaga is the greatest of all because it gives you peace instantaneously. As soon as you give up the anxiety for the fruits of actions, your mind will stop agitating.
Most of my agitations are about the fruits -- fear of what will happen in the future. Bhagavan said, once you give that up, peace will come automatically. Therefore it is greater than anything.
So Bhakti is like an HOV lane on the highway. It takes you to your destination much quicker than other paths -- Karma Yoga, Gnana Yoga, Dhyana Yoga. Those are slower paths.
There are several entry points you can have. Either you are ready and give your mind to me. If youre not ready, keep practicing.
If not, keep working for me. If not, just give up the fruits of actions and you will be my Bhakta. And then in the last few verses, starting from verse 13, weve seen the nature, the characteristics, the qualities of a perfect devotee.
All our preconceived notions about a bhakta -- that he has given up everything and is just doing nothing but bhajans all day long. And as used to say, with those noisy accompaniments -- no, thats not bhakti. A Bhakta is the one who has these qualities.
So Bhagavan has given the litmus test of who is a perfect devotee. And 36 qualities of a perfect devotee, starting from Adveshta Sarvabhutanam Maitrah Karunayevacha. One who does not hate anyone.
As I said, it is so difficult for us to even have that concept, because so many things in this world we dont like. As long as you have identification with this body, mind, and intellect -- within the realm of this body, this mind, this intellect -- anything which is not conducive to the body, Ill hate. Its too hot, its too cold -- because its not conducive to my body. When I used to live in Nairobi, you didnt need air conditioning or heating.
The city by nature is perfectly air-conditioned -- the temperature remains between 65 and 75 all throughout the year. So I found that very conducive, a good city to live in. Until we found out that Meena and my son Neeraj both had asthma because of the high altitude.
So for me it was very conducive. For them it was completely not conducive. So Bhagavan says, as long as you identify with this body, mind, and intellect, there will be things that are mentally conducive and sometimes mentally not conducive, intellectually conducive and intellectually not conducive.
But one who is not identified with these limitations -- for him it becomes possible to worship God without any form. A true Bhakta reaches that point. So we have been seeing these qualities from the last few verses.
Samah shatrau cha mitre cha tatha mana apamana yoh, shitoshna sukha duhkheshu samah sanga vivarjitah. One who no longer considers this body and intellect to be me, but rather my equipment. For him, his relationships are neutral in all aspects.
Nobody is truly my friend and nobody is truly my foe. But there is a Vyavaharik (transactional) relationship I will have. The people who help me are my friends.
The people who hinder me are my enemies. But thats a Vyavaharik, transactional relationship. But at the core of my being, I remain equanimous to them.
As long as I identify with my mind, there will be honor and dishonor. Obviously, we architects put our buildings out for all to see. They say that doctors bury their mistakes; we put ours out for the world to see.
The buildings I dont like, I avoid passing by. The ones I like, I make sure to pass by -- because at the intellectual level, honor and dishonor is what I perceive. But you see, for the true Bhakta, both are equal.
Shitoshna sukha duhkheshu -- at the body level, hot and cold. That does not mean I dont feel hot. Somebody asked Gurudev, Why is it that you always go in the best car? Because people would go to pick up at the airport.
Someone has a Mercedes or BMW or Lexus. There are people who have Toyotas. You dont go in those cars. said, Im not stupid. If the best car is available, which is more reliable and not going to break down on the way, why should I take a chance and go in an old Subaru that may break down on the highway? So when it is available to me to mitigate discomfort at the body level, I will do it.
But if it is not available, I persevere and continue. Shitoshna sukha duhkha -- Agamapayinah, Anityah -- they come and go. I remain constantly at peace because Samah Sanga Vivarjitah -- I remain constantly in a state of equanimity because Im not attached to any of these worlds of mine.
Physical, mental, intellectual. Tulya ninda stutih mauni -- Tulya ninda stutih means equanimous to criticism and praise. Because no matter what you do, somebody will praise the same act and somebody will criticize that same act.
The Supreme Court takes a decision on those abortion pills. Democrats are rejoicing -- They did the right thing. Republicans are saying, What is this court doing? So Ninda and Stuti, criticism and praise -- both I consider to be not about my actions alone but a reflection of their mental environment. Somebody will like what I say because it is conducive to them.
Somebody will criticize what I say because it is not conducive to them. Therefore, a true devotee of the Lord -- in other words, one who has identified himself with the supreme -- remains at peace in all situations. Mauni -- he becomes silent, not just physically or at the speech level.
At the mind level, I may be silent but fuming inside. And thats very dangerous. You can end up in trouble if you dont vocalize your anger, dont vocalize your ideas, dont vocalize whats going on in your mind.
But this is silence at the mind level. When Mauni, the true devotee, becomes silent at the mind level -- that is true silence. Santushtah yena kenachit -- content with this or that, content with whatever comes.

These concluding verses of Chapter 12 offer the culminating portrait of the beloved devotee. Tulya-ninda-stutih, equal to censure and praise. The teaching observes that no matter what we do, some will praise and some will criticize. The same Supreme Court decision causes Democrats to rejoice and Republicans to despair. This recognition can liberate us from the exhausting effort to please everyone. The devotee understands that praise and blame reflect the mental state of others more than objective truth about ourselves. Mauni, one who has become silent, not merely at the level of speech but at the level of mind. This inner silence is the fruit of true devotion.
Santushto yena kenacit, content with whatever comes. Aniketah, without a fixed abode. This does not mean homelessness but freedom from psychological dependence on any particular place, possession, or circumstance for ones sense of security. The devotee is at home everywhere because the Divine is everywhere. Sthira-matih, steady-minded. The mind that has found its anchor in the infinite does not sway with every passing wind of circumstance.
The final verse (20) brings it all together: those who pursue this dharmy-amritam (immortal righteousness) with shraddha (faith), making the Divine their supreme goal, are ativa me priyah, exceedingly dear to the Lord. Bhakti, we learn, is like an HOV lane on the highway of spiritual progress, it takes us faster to our destination than other paths. Today, choose one quality from these verses that feels most distant from your current state: Is it contentment? Silence of mind? Equanimity toward praise and blame? Freedom from fixed attachments? Do not judge yourself for the gap, but use it as a compass pointing toward growth. What one small step could you take today in that direction?
